sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wished arrays had superpowers? The `Arrays` class is here to save the day! It’s like a Swiss Army knife for arrays in Java.

• How to sort, search, and compare arrays effortlessly
• Ways to fill, copy, and convert arrays in one line
• Practical tricks to make your code cleaner and faster

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re organizing a bookshelf. You could manually sort each book by title, but wouldn’t it be easier if someone handed you a magic wand to do it instantly? That’s what the `Arrays` class does for your arrays!

The `Arrays` class is a **utility class** in Java’s `java.util` package. It provides static methods to perform common operations on arrays—like sorting, searching, and filling—without writing loops or complex logic.

• **No need to reinvent the wheel**: Why write a sorting algorithm when `Arrays.sort()` exists?
• **Works with all array types**: Primitives (`int[]`, `double[]`) and objects (`String[]`, `Integer[]`).
• **Saves time and reduces bugs**: Less code = fewer mistakes.

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Arrays.sort() sorts an array in ascending order in place
Arrays.binarySearch() finds an element in a sorted array and returns its index
Arrays.toString() returns a human-readable string representation of the array
Arrays.equals() compares two arrays element by element for equality
Arrays.fill() sets every element in the array to a specified value

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The `Arrays` class is your shortcut for common array operations—no loops needed. Always sort before searching (`binarySearch` only works on sorted arrays). Practice with `sort()`, `fill()`, and `equals()` to write cleaner code.

questions.question: Which method from the Arrays class converts an array to a readable string?
questions.explanation: Arrays.toString(arr) returns a string representation of the array in the format [elem1, elem2, elem3]. This is useful for printing array contents.

questions.question: What does Arrays.fill(arr, value) do?
options: Assigns the specified value to every element in the array
Finds the value in the array
Removes the value from the array
questions.explanation: Arrays.fill(arr, value) sets every element in the array to the specified value. For example, Arrays.fill(arr, 0) sets all elements to 0.
